author: TEDx Talks
description:
When dinner begins with a screen, what happens to the experience of dining itself? Shruthi Manjula Balakrishna examines how QR code menus and digital convenience are quietly reshaping taste, conversation, and human connection. Blending design, behavior, and humor, this talk reveals how technology may be changing far more than just how we order. Originally from Bangalore, India, and now based in Austin, Texas, Shruthi Manjula Balakrishna is Director of Research & Design at FÖDA, where she leads research-driven brand and experience work for global brands, cultural institutions, and hospitality clients, making human behavior feel a bit more understandable. As a Doctor of Design candidate at NC State University, she investigates how crisis reshapes consumption and how design quietly nudges what we notice, value, buy, and how we behave.

author: TEDx Talks
description: This talk explores what happens to our natural curiosity as we grow older—and how we gradually stop asking the questions that help us understand ourselves, others, and the world around us. It invites us to look beyond statements such as “I can’t,” “I’m terrible at maths,” or “My child doesn’t listen” and ask the more meaningful question: why? Through the idea of a “Why Swap,” the talk shows how reframing our assumptions can change the way we learn, communicate, and respond to challenges. It concludes with a simple challenge: ask one meaningful “why” every day for seven days and see what changes. An economist by training and an educator by vocation, Deepika Jain is the founder of Prep Right, an early learning initiative committed to reimagining childhood education. A graduate of Welham Girls' School, Lady Shri Ram College, Delhi, and Warwick Business School, UK, she has spent the past seven years studying neuroscience, child psychology, and international educational practices. title: Why Do We Stop Asking Why? | Deepika Jain | TEDxStrawberry Fields High School

author: TEDx Talks
description: Permission to Re(Define) traces the “permission slip” across accent, embodied expression and academic identity. Through personal anecdotes, Fricker’s epistemic injustice and Goffman’s theory of stigma, it attempts to expose how an arbitrary idea of “normal” disciplines us into shrinking and conforming. The talk ultimately rejects that bargain, reclaiming self-definition as an act of defiance. At 17, Arnav Ghai is a recent IBDP graduate and an incoming engineering student whose interests span ideation, storytelling and performance. A published researcher and enthusiastic creative writer with years of theatre experience, he is deeply interested in doodling margin cartoons, befriending dogs, watching canonical coming-of-age movies, and understanding how identity is shaped in various socio-cultural contexts. Drawing on personal experience, in his talk Arnav examines how ‘normality’ is constructed and internalised, and what becomes possible when we reclaim the authority to define ourselve
title: The Permission to Re(Define) | Arnav Ghai | TEDxStrawberry Fields High School

In his talk, Adam shows and tells us how the arts and theatre can themselves be a vessel for turning the individual into a community, and how the arts have always been telling us about the very community we live in. From performing since the age of four to shaping stories across theatre, film, and digital media, Adam brings a unique voice that sits between humour and discomfort, exploring identity, belonging, and the unspoken.
With standout performances in Bocci: Il-Musical and Kif Tgħallimt Insuq, and as an award-winning producer behind I Wish I Never Existed, his work challenges audiences to reflect and feel. description:
What if the biggest costs in an organization are the ones that never appear on an invoice?

Through the story of Adam and the “small holes” that quietly develop before a major failure, this talk explores the hidden cost of unreported incidents, neglected maintenance, and overlooked safety risks. It challenges organizations to rethink safety not as an expense or compliance requirement, but as a strategic investment in people, productivity, and long-term growth.

The talk ultimately asks leaders to change their perspective before a small problem becomes a major loss—because sustainable progress begins with noticing what others overlook. Shailendra Vispute is a seasoned operations leader with over three decades of experience in the chemical manufacturing industry. title: The Cost of What We Don't See | Shailender Vispute | TEDxMoulsari Avenue

author: TEDx Talks
description:
AI is making execution faster—but what should we do with the time it gives back?

This talk introduces the idea of the “Thinking Budget”: deliberately reinvesting the time saved through AI-powered execution into deeper thinking, creativity, learning, and problem-solving. Rather than using technology simply to produce more, the speaker argues that its greatest value lies in giving people the space to think better.

By challenging the traditional trade-offs between quality, speed, and cost, the talk explores how AI can change the way we approach work—and potentially allow us to optimize all three while creating better outcomes. Arpit Bhatia is a product design leader with 10+ years of experience across fintech, consumer tech, social commerce, travel tech, ed tech, and media. We often make life-changing decisions without knowing why—and only understand their meaning years later. This talk explores how purpose, continuous improvement, and acceptance can help us make sense of choices, struggles, and unexpected turns in life.

Through personal experiences of leaving a secure career, responding to unexpected challenges, and embracing new opportunities, the speaker reveals how what seems like uncertainty in the moment can become clarity in retrospect. The talk invites us to reconsider how we view our past—not as a series of random events, but as experiences whose meaning can gradually unfold. Dr Nandiki Gangadhar Reddy is a CEO and Managing Partner of Dongyue Engineering and Fabricators. He is an engineer-turned-entrepreneur, green activist, industrial innovator, actor, and film producer. title: The meaning we find later | Dr. Nandiki Gangadhar Reddy | TEDxMoulsari Avenue

author: TEDx Talks
description:
This talk explores the power of narratives to shape what we believe, accept as true, and ultimately how we see the world. Beginning with a deliberately convincing argument about smoking, it demonstrates how confidence, emotion, repetition, and identity can make even a fabricated story feel real. The talk then examines how narratives operate in society, particularly through political discourse, media, and everyday language, showing how repeated stories can become accepted as common sense. It concludes with a call for intellectual freedom: to recognise the narratives influencing us, hold competing stories side by side, and become more conscious of the stories we ourselves pass on. Suhail is driven by curiosity and a desire to understand how ideas shape the way we see the world. Fascinated by the questions behind our beliefs, he explores why certain stories endure, how narratives influence our thinking, and what happens when we learn to question them.

title: Narratives | Suhail Shadab | TEDxStrawberry Fields High School

author: TEDx Talks
description: A deeply personal journey of loss, resilience, and transformation, this talk explores how a single life-changing experience can completely reshape the way we see suffering and adversity. Through the story of losing her mother at a young age and witnessing her father’s battle with illness, the speaker reflects on how what once seemed like punishment gradually revealed itself as protection and purpose. The talk challenges us to look beyond our immediate circumstances, embrace uncertainty, and recognise the preciousness of life. Ultimately, it is a reminder that while we may not always be able to change what happens to us, we can choose the perspective through which we experience it—and that shift can change everything. Dr Meghna Gupta, a renowned aesthetic dermatologist and wellness mentor, has always believed that the most meaningful transformations are not just of the skin but of the self. description: The talk explores how constantly telling young people they will “do great things” in the future can unintentionally teach them to wait rather than act. Drawing on psychological research and a personal experience, it examines how expectations, future-oriented thinking, and the need for permission can shape young people’s sense of agency. The speaker argues that being a changemaker does not require extraordinary achievements, but begins with small, deliberate actions in the present. The talk ultimately challenges young people to replace “I’m going to…” with “What can I do today?” Sumayah Mittal is a recent IB Diploma graduate and Valedictorian from Strawberry Fields High School, where she served as School Captain. She will be pursuing Psychology with Education at University College London. title: How we teach young people to wait | Sumayah Mittal | TEDxStrawberry Fields High School

author: TEDx Talks
description:
In this talk, Mansimar Kaur explores the relationship between storytelling and self-perception — asking what truly makes you you. She examines the tension between "the story I tell myself" (am I capable, powerful, a leader, an outsider?) and "the story others tell about me" (shaped by family, community, culture, and expectations), arguing that identity lives somewhere in the tension between the two.
Kaur grounds this exploration in real-world stakes: from the intimate act of stitching and craft as a form of storytelling, to the lived experience of displacement (as seen in flood-affected communities), to the state of narrative freedom itself — citing India's 2025 World Press Freedom Index ranking of 151/180 and 65 documented internet shutdowns in India in 2025 as evidence of how access to voice and story is contested at a societal level.

title: "Why Does Storytelling Shape Identity?" | Mansimar Kaur | TEDxStrawberry Fields High School

Tejasvin believes that young people are not only the leaders of tomorrow but active contributors to change today. In his role as School Captain and as the Director-General of the SFHS Model United Nations Conference 2026, he has developed a strong commitment to leadership, dialogue, and public service. description: Prarthana Lumba's talk, "Stories That Shape History: Whose Voice Counts?", examines how dominant narratives are shaped by covert power dynamics that reinforce gender binaries and present a single "official" reality, silencing marginalized voices — particularly women in the Global South — through what Gayatri Spivak calls "epistemic violence." Drawing on the metaphor of the Panopticon, she shows how surveillance breeds self-censorship, illustrating this with field quotes from rural women in Karauli, Tikamgarh, Chitrakoot, Patalkot, and Chhattisgarh who describe feeling voiceless, linguistically excluded from formal spaces, and conditioned into subservience. She argues that researchers must practice positionality and reflexivity, using tools like Feminist Participatory Action Research (FPAR) to bridge the gap between researcher and community rather than extract from it, closing with a call — echoing Mao Zedong — to learn from and build alongside the people whose stories are so often lef
title: Shaping Dominant Narratives | Prarthana Lumba | TEDxStrawberry Fields High School

description:
Asav explores what it means to belong when you find yourself between cultures, identities, and worlds. His journey from India to Caltech revealed an unexpected paradox: leaving home can offer the freedom we seek, while simultaneously making us strangers in places where we once felt certain of who we were.

Through personal stories of navigating cultural differences, an unexpected Thanksgiving invitation from a professor, and his later experience welcoming newly arrived international students, Asav examines the difference between **permission, inclusion, and belonging**.

The talk argues that belonging is not something we simply find; it is something we create together. It has two authors—the person willing to arrive without erasing themselves, and the person inside the room willing to notice them and make space.

title: Belonging begins with an invitation | Asav Kumar | TEDxStrawberry Fields High School

This talk explores how the way we attend to the world shapes the world we actually live in. Drawing from neuroscience, philosophy and cultural critique, Moran argues that attention is not just a matter of focus, it is the foundation of meaning, love, and moral life itself. He shows how modern civilization built on the narrow, grasping mode of attention, has led us into “Error 404: World Not Found,” a state where we mistake representations for reality. Through stories, science, and reflection, Moran calls for a renewal of what he calls “right attention,” a way of seeing that is receptive rather than possessive, present rather than distracted, and ultimately the last line of defense
